nodes.name: Dirichlet character
nodes.statement: A Dirichlet character modulo $n$ is a group homomorphism $\chi \colon (\mathbb{Z} / n \mathbb{Z})^\times \to \mathbb{C}^\times$. One can easily extend a Dirichlet character to a function $\chi \colon \mathbb{Z} \ra \mathbb{C}^\times$ by the rules $$ \chi(a) = 0 \text{ if } (a, n) \ne 1, \quad \chi(a + n) = \chi(a). $$ We use this last definition throughout.
nodes.statement_short: A group homomorphism $(\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times\to\mathbb{C}^\times$, extended to $\mathbb{Z}$ by zero on non-units and periodicity.
nodes.label: defn:dirichlet_character

nodes.name: Conductor of a Dirichlet character
nodes.statement: The conductor of a Dirichlet character $\chi$ is the smallest positive integer $f$ such that $\chi(a + f) = \chi(a)$.
differentia: smallest positive integer $f$ such that $\chi(a + f) = \chi(a)$
nodes.label: defn:conductor_dirchar

nodes.name: Gauss sum
nodes.statement: Let $\chi$ be a Dirichlet character modulo $f$. The Gauss sum of $\chi$ is defined as $$ \tau(\chi) = \sum_{a = 1}^f \chi(a) \zeta_f^a, $$ where $\zeta_f$ is a primitive $f$th root of unity.
nodes.statement_short: $\tau(\chi)=\sum_a \chi(a)\zeta_f^a$ for a character mod $f$.
nodes.label: defn:gauss_sum

nodes.name: Dirichlet L-series
nodes.statement: Let $\chi$ be a Dirichlet character of conductor $f$ and let $L(s, \chi)$ be the Dirichlet $L$-series attached to $\chi$.

nodes.name: Value of Dirichlet L-series at s=1
nodes.statement: We have $$ L(1, \chi) = \begin{cases} -\frac{\tau(\chi)}{f} \sum_{a = 1}^{f} \overline{\chi}(a) \log | (1 - \zeta_f)^a | & \text{ if } \chi(-1) = 1, \ \chi \ne 1, \\ \pi i \frac{\tau(\chi)}{f} \cdot \frac{1}{f} \sum_{a = 1}^f \overline{\chi}(a)a & \text{ if } \chi(-1) = -1. \end{cases} $$
assumptions: Let $\chi$ be a Dirichlet character of conductor $f$ and let $L(s, \chi)$ be the Dirichlet $L$-series attached to $\chi$.
nodes.statement_short: Closed formula for $L(1,\chi)$ via Gauss sums: log of cyclotomic units for even $\chi\ne1$, a character sum for odd $\chi$.
nodes.label: thm:L_series_sum_log_units

nodes.name: Character times Gauss sum identity
nodes.statement: For every integer $b$, we have $$ \chi(b) \tau(\overline{\chi}) = \sum_{a = 1}^f \overline{\chi}(a) e^{\frac{2\pi i a b}{f}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: $\chi(b)\tau(\bar\chi)$ equals the twisted exponential sum $\sum_a\bar\chi(a)e^{2\pi iab/f}$.
nodes.label: lem:chi_gauss_sum

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Using Lemma~\ref{lem:chi_gauss_sum} and the definition of the Dirichlet $L$-series, we write \begin{eqnarray*} L(1, \chi) &=& \sum_{n = 1}^{\infty} \frac{\chi(n)}{n} = \sum_{n = 1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n} \frac{1}{\tau(\overline{\chi})} \sum_{a = 1}^f \overline{\chi}(a) e^{2\pi i a n / f} = \\ &=& \frac{1}{\tau(\overline{\chi})} \sum_{a = 1}^f \overline{\chi}(a) \sum_{n = 1}^{\infty} \frac{e^{2\pi i a n / f}}{n} = \\ &=& - \frac{1}{\tau(\overline{\chi})} \sum_{a = 1}^f \overline{\chi}(a) \log(1 - \zeta_f^a). \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\chi(n)$ via Lemma 1 into exponentials, swap sums, and sum the series $\sum e^{2\pi i an/f}/n=-\log(1-\zeta_f^a)$.

nodes.name: Number field signature and unit rank
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a number field with $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex embeddings and let $r = r_1 + r_2 - 1$.

nodes.name: Independent units
nodes.statement: Let $\epsilon_1, \dots, \epsilon_r$ be a set of independent units of $L$.

nodes.name: Real and complex embeddings
nodes.statement: Let $\sigma_1, \dots, \sigma_{r_1}$ be the set of real embeddings and let $(\sigma_{r_1 + 1}, \overline{\sigma}_{r_1 + 1}), \dots, (\sigma_{r}, \overline{\sigma}_{r})$ be the pairs of conjugate complex embeddings.
nodes.label: defn:mixed_embeddings

nodes.name: Regulator
nodes.statement: We define the regulator of the units $\epsilon_1, \dots, \epsilon_r$ of $L$ as $$ R_L(\epsilon_1, \dots, \epsilon_r) := \sqrt{\det(\delta_{i} \log | \sigma_i(\epsilon_j) | )_{i, j}}, $$ where $$ \delta_i = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{ if } \sigma_i \text{ is real}, \\ 2 & \text{ if } \sigma_i \text{ is complex}. \end{cases} $$
nodes.statement_short: $R_L(\epsilon)$ is the square root of the determinant of $(\delta_i\log|\sigma_i(\epsilon_j)|)$, $\delta_i=1$ or $2$ for real/complex $\sigma_i$.
nodes.label: defn:regulator

nodes.name: Index of unit subgroups equals ratio of regulators
nodes.statement: Let $\epsilon_1, \dots, \epsilon_r$ be independent units of a number field $K$ that generate a subgroup $A$ of the units of $K$ modulo roots of unity and let $\eta_1, \dots, \eta_r$ generate a subgroup $B$. If $A \subseteq B$ is of finite index then $$ [B : A] = \frac{R_K(\epsilon_1, \dots, \epsilon_r)}{R_K(\eta_1, \dots, \eta_r)}. $$
nodes.section: 3.2 The index of units subgroups and regulators
assumptions: Let $\epsilon_1, \dots, \epsilon_r$ be independent units of a number field $K$ that generate a subgroup $A$ of the units of $K$ modulo roots of unity
nodes.statement_short: For finite-index unit subgroups $A\subseteq B$, $[B:A]$ is the ratio of their regulators.
nodes.label: lem:index_eq_reg_ratio

nodes.name: Smith normal form
nodes.statement: Let $M \in \GL_{n \times m}(\mathbb{Z})$ be an integer matrix. There exists matrices $U \in \GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$ and $V \in \GL_m(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $$ U M V = \begin{pmatrix} D & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} $$ where $D = \textrm{diag}(d_1, \dots, d_r)$ is an $r \times r$ diagonal integer matrix with $d_1 \mid d_2 \mid \dots \mid d_r$.
nodes.section: 3.2 The index of units subgroups and regulators
assumptions: Let $M \in \GL_{n \times m}(\mathbb{Z})$ be an integer matrix.
conclusions: There exists matrices $U \in \GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$ and $V \in \GL_m(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $$ U M V = \begin{pmatrix} D & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} $$ where $D = \textrm{diag}(d_1, \dots, d_r)$ is an $r \times r$ diagonal integer matrix with $d_1 \mid d_2 \mid \dots \mid d_r$.
nodes.statement_short: Every integer matrix is equivalent over $\mathbb{Z}$ to a diagonal matrix with divisibility chain $d_1\mid\cdots\mid d_r$.
nodes.label: lem:elem_divisors

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Since $A \subseteq B$, one can write $$ \eta_i = \epsilon_1^{a_{i1}} \cdot \dots \cdot \epsilon_r^{a_{i r}} \cdot \mu^{(i)}, \quad i = 1, \dots, r, $$ where $a_{ij} \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $\mu^{(i)}$ is a root of unity. By taking absolute values and logarithms, $$ \delta_j \log | \sigma_j(\eta_i) | = \sum_{k = 1}^r a_{ik} \delta_j \log | \sigma_j(\epsilon_k) |, \quad i = 1, \dots, r. $$ Therefore, using Defintiion~\ref{defn:regulator}, we have \begin{equation} \frac{R_K(\epsilon_1, \dots, \epsilon_r)}{R_K(\eta_1, \dots, \eta_r)} = \det ((a_{ik})_{i, k = 1}^r) \end{equation} Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:elem_divisors}, we can find matrices $U, V \in \GL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $$ U (a_{ik})_{i, k = 1}^r V = \text{diag}(d_1, \dots, d_r). $$ Therefore, changing the basis of $A$ and $B$ with $M$ and $N$, respectively, we obtain bases $x_1, \dots, x_r$ of $A$ and $y_1, \dots, y_r$ of $B$ such that $x_i = d_i y_i$, i.e., $$ B / A = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^r \mathbb{Z} / d_i \mathbb{Z}. $$ Hence, $[B : A] = |\prod_{i = 1}^r d_i | = \det ((a_{ik})_{i, k = 1}^r)$ which, combined with \eqref{eq:reg_ratio}, proves the lemma.
nodes.section: 3.2 The index of units subgroups and regulators
nodes.statement_short: Express the $\eta_i$ in the $\epsilon_k$, so the regulator ratio is $\det(a_{ik})$; Smith normal form shows this determinant is $[B:A]$.

nodes.name: Regulator ratio as determinant
nodes.statement: \frac{R_K(\epsilon_1, \dots, \epsilon_r)}{R_K(\eta_1, \dots, \eta_r)} = \det ((a_{ik})_{i, k = 1}^r)
nodes.section: 3.2 The index of units subgroups and regulators
nodes.statement_short: Ratio of regulators equals $\det(a_{ik})$.
nodes.label: eq:reg_ratio

nodes.name: Express η in terms of ε
nodes.statement: Since $A \subseteq B$, one can write $$ \eta_i = \epsilon_1^{a_{i1}} \cdot \dots \cdot \epsilon_r^{a_{i r}} \cdot \mu^{(i)}, \quad i = 1, \dots, r, $$ where $a_{ij} \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $\mu^{(i)}$ is a root of unity.
nodes.section: 3.2 The index of units subgroups and regulators
nodes.statement_short: Write each $\eta_i$ as a product of powers of the $\epsilon_k$ times a root of unity.

nodes.name: Take logs of absolute values
nodes.statement: By taking absolute values and logarithms, $$ \delta_j \log | \sigma_j(\eta_i) | = \sum_{k = 1}^r a_{ik} \delta_j \log | \sigma_j(\epsilon_k) |, \quad i = 1, \dots, r. $$
nodes.section: 3.2 The index of units subgroups and regulators
nodes.statement_short: Linear relation among the log-embedding vectors.

nodes.name: Regulator ratio as determinant
nodes.statement: Therefore, using Defintiion~\ref{defn:regulator}, we have \begin{equation} \frac{R_K(\epsilon_1, \dots, \epsilon_r)}{R_K(\eta_1, \dots, \eta_r)} = \det ((a_{ik})_{i, k = 1}^r) \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.2 The index of units subgroups and regulators
nodes.statement_short: By the regulator definition, the ratio is $\det(a_{ik})$.

nodes.name: Apply Smith normal form
nodes.statement: Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:elem_divisors}, we can find matrices $U, V \in \GL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $$ U (a_{ik})_{i, k = 1}^r V = \text{diag}(d_1, \dots, d_r). $$
nodes.section: 3.2 The index of units subgroups and regulators
nodes.statement_short: Diagonalize $(a_{ik})$ by Smith normal form.

nodes.name: Compute quotient B/A
nodes.statement: Therefore, changing the basis of $A$ and $B$ with $M$ and $N$, respectively, we obtain bases $x_1, \dots, x_r$ of $A$ and $y_1, \dots, y_r$ of $B$ such that $x_i = d_i y_i$, i.e., $$ B / A = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^r \mathbb{Z} / d_i \mathbb{Z}. $$
nodes.section: 3.2 The index of units subgroups and regulators
nodes.statement_short: Adapted bases give $B/A\cong\bigoplus\mathbb{Z}/d_i$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence, $[B : A] = |\prod_{i = 1}^r d_i | = \det ((a_{ik})_{i, k = 1}^r)$ which, combined with \eqref{eq:reg_ratio}, proves the lemma.
nodes.section: 3.2 The index of units subgroups and regulators
nodes.statement_short: Index equals $\prod d_i=\det(a_{ik})$, combined with (3.1).

nodes.name: Maximal real subfield K^+
nodes.statement: Let $K = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$ where $\zeta_n$ is a primitive $n$-th root of unit. Define the subfield $K^+ := \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n + \zeta_n^{-1})$ of $K$.
nodes.label: defn:K_plus

nodes.name: K^+ is the maximal real subfield
nodes.statement: The subfield $K^+$ is the maximal real subfield of $K$.
conclusions: The subfield $K^+$ is the maximal real subfield of $K$.
nodes.label: lem:K_plus_max_real_sub

nodes.name: Galois group of K^+
nodes.statement: The Galois group of $\Gal(K^+ / \mathbb{Q})$ is generated by the automorphisms $\sigma_a \colon \zeta \mapsto \zeta^a$ for $1 \leq a \leq p^m / 2$, $(a, p) = 1$.
conclusions: is generated by the automorphisms $\sigma_a \colon \zeta \mapsto \zeta^a$ for $1 \leq a \leq p^m / 2$, $(a, p) = 1$.
nodes.label: lem:gal_K_plus

nodes.name: Cyclotomic units
nodes.statement: Define the cyclotomic units of a cyclotomic field $K = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$ with ring of integers $O_K = \mathbb{Z}[\zeta_n]$ as the group $$ C_K := O_K^\times \cap \langle \zeta_n^a, 1 - \zeta_n^b \colon a, b \in \mathbb{Z} / n \mathbb{Z}\rangle. $$
nodes.statement_short: $C_K$ is the group of units of $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_n]$ generated by roots of unity and the $1-\zeta_n^b$.
nodes.label: defn:cyclo_units

nodes.name: Index of cyclotomic units equals class number of K^+
nodes.statement: Let $n := p^m \in \mathbb{N}$ for a prime $p$ and a positive integer $m$, and let $K = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$ where $\zeta_n$ is a primitive $n$-th root of unit. Let $O_K$ be the ring of integers of $K$. Let $C_K$ be the group of cyclotomic units in $K$ according to Definition~\ref{defn:cyclo_units}. Then \[ [O_{K^+}^\times : C_{K^+}] = h_{K^+}, \] where $h_{K^+}$ is the class number of the maximal real subfield $K^+$ of $K$.
assumptions: Let $n := p^m \in \mathbb{N}$ for a prime $p$ and a positive integer $m$, and let $K = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$ where $\zeta_n$ is a primitive $n$-th root of unit.
Let $O_K$ be the ring of integers of $K$.
Let $C_K$ be the group of cyclotomic units in $K$ according to Definition~\ref{defn:cyclo_units}.
conclusions: \[ [O_{K^+}^\times : C_{K^+}] = h_{K^+}, \] where $h_{K^+}$ is the class number of the maximal real subfield $K^+$ of $K$.
nodes.statement_short: For $n=p^m$, the index of the cyclotomic units in the units of $K^+$ equals the class number $h_{K^+}$.
nodes.label: thm:index_of_units

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2 (outline)
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item Show that the regulator of the units $\xi_a$ is non-zero, where $$ \xi_a := \zeta_{p^m}^{(1-a)/2} \frac{1 - \zeta_{p^m}^a}{1 - \zeta_{p^m}}, \qquad 1 \leq a < p^m / 2, \ (a, p) = 1. $$ \item Compute the regulator $R(\{\xi_a\})$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Outline: show the regulator of the units $\xi_a$ is nonzero, then compute $R(\{\xi_a\})$.

nodes.name: Regulator of ξ_a is non-zero
nodes.statement: Show that the regulator of the units $\xi_a$ is non-zero, where $$ \xi_a := \zeta_{p^m}^{(1-a)/2} \frac{1 - \zeta_{p^m}^a}{1 - \zeta_{p^m}}, \qquad 1 \leq a < p^m / 2, \ (a, p) = 1. $$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the units $\xi_a$ and show their regulator is non-zero.

nodes.name: Compute regulator of ξ_a
nodes.statement: Compute the regulator $R(\{\xi_a\})$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $R(\{\xi_a\})$.

nodes.name: Regulator of ξ_a equals h^+ R^+
nodes.statement: We have $$ R(\{\xi_a\}) = h^+ R^+, $$ where $R^+$ is the regulator of $K^+$.
conclusions: $$ R(\{\xi_a\}) = h^+ R^+, $$ where $R^+$ is the regulator of $K^+$.
nodes.statement_short: The regulator of the cyclotomic units $\xi_a$ is $h^+$ times the regulator of $K^+$.
nodes.label: lem:reg_Ra

nodes.name: Galois group G of K^+
nodes.statement: Let $G = \Gal(K^+ / \mathbb{Q})$.

nodes.name: Regulator of ξ_a as product of character sums
nodes.statement: We have $$ | R(\{\xi_a\}) | = \frac{1}{2} \left | \prod_{\substack{\chi \in \widehat{G} \\ \chi \ne 1}} \sum_{a = 1}^{p^m} \chi(a) \log |1 - \zeta^a| \right |. $$
nodes.statement_short: $|R(\{\xi_a\})|$ is half the product over nontrivial $\chi\in\hat G$ of $\sum_a\chi(a)\log|1-\zeta^a|$.
nodes.label: lem:reg_Ra_charsum

nodes.name: Product formula for cyclotomic units
nodes.statement: For any $1 \leq k < n$, we have $$ \prod_{\substack{1 \leq a < p^n \\ a \equiv b \bmod p^k}} (1 - \zeta_{p^n}^a) = 1 - \zeta_{p^k}^b. $$
nodes.statement_short: Product of $1-\zeta_{p^n}^a$ over $a\equiv b \bmod p^k$ equals $1-\zeta_{p^k}^b$.
nodes.label: lem:prod_cycl_units

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8
nodes.statement: We rewrite $$ \prod_{\substack{1 \leq a < p^n \\ a \equiv b \bmod p^k}} (1 - \zeta_{p^n}^a) = \prod_{s = 0}^{p^{n-k}-1}(1 - \zeta_{p^n}^b \zeta_{p^{n-k}}^s) = 1 - \zeta_{p^k}^b, $$ where the last equality follows from $$ \prod_{i = 0}^{m-1} (1 - \zeta_m^i x)= x^m \prod_{i = 0}^{m-1} (x^{-1} - \zeta_m^i) = x^m (x^{-m} - 1) = 1 - x^m $$ applied to $m = p^{n-k}$ and $x = \zeta_{p^n}^b$.
nodes.statement_short: Reindex the product over a coset and apply $\prod_i(1-\zeta_m^i x)=1-x^m$ with $m=p^{n-k}$, $x=\zeta_{p^n}^b$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6 (incomplete)
nodes.statement: First, for a Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $p^n$ of conductor $f_{\chi} = p^k$ for some $1 \leq k < n$, Lemma~\ref{lem:prod_cycl_units} yields $$ \prod_{\substack{1 \leq a < p^n \\ a \equiv b \bmod p^k}} (1 - \zeta_{p^n}^a) = 1 - \zeta_{p^n}^b. $$ Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:reg_Ra_charsum} and Theorem~\ref{thm:L_series_sum_log_units}, we obtain \begin{eqnarray*} R(\{\xi_a\}) &=& \frac{1}{2} \left | \prod_{\chi \in \widehat{G}, \chi \ne 1} \sum_{a = 1}^{p^n} \chi(a) \log |1 - \zeta^a| \right | = \\ &=& \frac{1}{2} \prod_{\chi \in \widehat{G}, \chi \ne 1} \sum_{a = 1}^{p^m} \chi(a) \log |1 - \zeta^a| = \\ \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Use Lemma 8 for characters of smaller conductor, then Lemma 7 and Theorem 1 to rewrite $R(\{\xi_a\})$ via $L(1,\chi)$ (unfinished).
